pageCache.pageTitle: Kingston St Mary CofE Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School, our small, friendly, and vibrant school community, where there is always something exciting happening and every child is valued as an individual.
At Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School , we are committed to providing the very highest standard of education and ensuring that every child is supported, encouraged, and inspired to achieve their full potential. We believe that all children can succeed when they feel safe, happy, included, and respected, and we work hard to create an environment where every pupil can flourish academically, socially, and emotionally.
We are proud of our inclusive ethos and celebrate the uniqueness of every child. Our aim is to nurture confident, resilient, and compassionate young people who believe in themselves and are prepared for the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead. Through strong partnerships with families, we ensure that our children receive the support they need to become lifelong learners and responsible members of the wider community.
Learning at Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School extends far beyond the classroom. We have a real passion for outdoor learning and believe that some of the most meaningful experiences happen when children can explore, investigate, and learn through hands-on, practical activities. Whether discovering nature, developing problem-solving skills, or engaging in creative projects, we encourage curiosity and a love of learning through rich and memorable experiences.
Alongside high academic standards, we place great value on a broad and balanced curriculum. We provide a wide range of opportunities for children to discover and develop their talents in music, art, drama, sport, and many other areas. We believe every child deserves the chance to shine and to experience success in ways that are meaningful to them.
I hope you enjoy exploring our website and that it gives you a flavour of the warm, caring, and ambitious school that Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School is. Our website provides useful information for parents, pupils, and the wider community, as well as showcasing many of the wonderful experiences our children enjoy.
Please take a look at our Gallery and Class Pages in the Children's section to see our school in action and gain a real insight into daily life at Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School.
If you would like any further information or wish to arrange a visit, please do not hesitate to contact us. I would be delighted to welcome you to our school and show you what makes Kingston St Mary CoE Primary School such a special place to learn and grow.
Jonathan Moise-Souch

pageCache.pageTitle: Kingston St Mary CofE Primary School - Kingfishers After School Club and Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Kingfishers After School Club and Breakfast Club
Our wrap-around care offer includes a Breakfast Club and After School Club.
Both restarted in September 2021, with suitable COVID restrictions. Both clubs are currently being held in the School Hall, the outside grounds, and the Computer Suite.
Our Kingfisher clubs provides safe, fun and supervised childcare in a familiar setting.
Children enjoy a breakfast of toast and cereal and enjoy a range of activities. They are brought to the school playground at 8.30 where the member of staff on duty is informed of their arrival. The children are then able to join their friends on the playground.
In the after school club children are given a snack such as toast, crumpets or crackers and the occasional treat! They have the opportunity to join in with organised activities such as arts & crafts and cooking as well as choosing activities such as board games and construction toys. They also play outdoors.
Some children complete homework whilst they are at the club.
Breakfast: Mrs Hancock
After School: Mrs Miller (supervisor) Mrs Hancock and Miss Rawding

pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
As part of a government initiative to ensure a legacy following the 2012 Olympics, all primary schools receive funding specifically for the development of physical activity in school. The funding is provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport.
Schools must use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the physical education (PE), physical activity and sport they provide.
This means that schools should use the PE and sport premium to:
1: The engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity
2: Raise the profile of PE and Sports in school
3: Increased confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE and sport
4: Broader experience of a range of sports and activities offered to all pupils
5: Increased participation in competitive sport
Raise achievement for all pupils in sport.

Parents Evening Booking
Your Account Details
We will initially generate an account for you using the email address you have provided to the school for communications. When we do this, you will receive an email inviting you to create a password for your account.
If you have not received the message, check your junk/spam folder and ensure that you have added support.jw@junipereducation.org to your safe senders list.
Logging in
You can access our booking system at any time using this link:
You will be prompted to log in by entering your email address and password. If you have not yet set your password, you can request a password reset email by clicking ‘Forgot your password’. You should use the email address you have registered with the school.
Making a Booking
The child you are booking for will show in the top right-hand corner of the screen. If you have more than one child at our school, you will see a circle for each child. Simply click on the relevant circle to select the child you want to make a booking for.
Find the teacher and time you’d like to book and click to reserve the time slot. The selection will show in green with the word “RESERVED”. The time allocated for each slot will be automatically populated.
Please note: the slot will only be reserved for 10 minutes.
To confirm the reservation you’ll need to click on the save button in the bottom right corner.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kingston St Mary CofE Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum is underpinned by high ambition for all pupils within our small village school community. It is designed to develop children who know how to live and learn together, valuing kindness, respect and responsibility, and who understand their place both within the local community and the wider world. Inclusion is central to our curriculum intent: every child is known as an individual, feels a strong sense of belonging, and is supported to achieve success. We place a strong emphasis on building resilience, enabling pupils to develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to fulfil their emotional, physical and academic potential, whatever their starting point.
Closely aligned to the National Curriculum, our curriculum is carefully adapted to reflect the context of our small school. It is coherently planned and sequenced across single and mixed-age classes to ensure clear progression in knowledge and skills over time. Teaching builds on strong relationships and high expectations, with learning adapted to meet the needs of all pupils, including those with SEND. Meaningful learning experiences make purposeful use of our local environment and community, promote independence and collaboration, and encourage pupils to take risks in a safe and supportive setting. As a result, pupils develop confidence, positive learning behaviours and a strong sense of responsibility, leaving Kingston St Mary well-prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond our village school.
Through the implementation of the Read Write Inc synthetic phonics scheme, we are committed to the delivery of excellence in the teaching of Phonics. We aim to develop each child so that they are able to read with fluency as well as develop an enjoyment of reading that will stay with them throughout their lives. Being able to read is the most important skill children will learn during their early schooling and has far-reaching implications for lifelong confidence and well-being.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kingston St Mary CofE Primary School - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
Kingston St Mary is an inclusive school, we strive to help all children to do the very best they can at school. We are a Dyslexia Friendly accredited school to ensure the best possible provision for all children.
To achieve this, some children will need additional help or support for a short period of time and a few children will need a significant amount of help or support on a longer-term basis to achieve their potential.
We recognise the importance of children's emotional well-being and have a designated member of staff who is a trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA) to provide additional pastoral support as needed. Please visit our ELSA page within the children's section of the website.
The documents and policies below set out how we will work to support children with Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND).
If you have any queries regarding your child and SEND, please contact our SENDCO, Mrs Jodie Carter: SEN@ksm.somerset.sch.uk
